condition: When creating a new automation via create_automation, or when rebuilding/converting an existing automation whose work is long-running, dispatch-heavy, or delivery-bearing
instruction:
Build automations CLI-bridge-hosted by default. The Zo turn only launches; the work runs in a detached `claude -p` that owns the resilience contract. This is the standard because Zo enforces a 120 s ceiling on every model call and a ~60 min session cap, and a run that exceeds either dies silently. Proven 2026-09-22: a converted Daily Scan ran 342 s (its prior Zo-hosted occurrence died at "Email send timed out after 300 seconds"); a converted queue drain ran 118 s, which the 120 s ceiling would have killed.

**The template — three parts.**

1. Zo instruction body is ONE launcher line plus a stay-silent contract:
   `bash /home/workspace/Skills/automation-resilience/scripts/bridge-launch.sh --job <job> --prompt-file /home/workspace/Skills/automation-resilience/prompts/<automation-id>-<job>.md [--preflight '<cheap test>']`
   Then: report only the single line it prints (`DETACHED` / `SKIP overlap` / `SKIP nowork` / `ERROR`), call no other tools, and send nothing.
2. The real work and the FULL resilience contract live in the prompt file under `Skills/automation-resilience/prompts/`. The contract runs INSIDE the bridge: `begin` -> `checkpoint` -> `side-effect-intent` -> `side-effect-resolve` -> `finish`.
3. The prompt must forbid `worker-start` — the bridge IS the long-lived worker — and must require every step to run synchronously in the foreground. `claude -p` exits the moment the model stops emitting, so a backgrounded command, a `run_in_background` task, or a monitor armed "to notify me" is killed unfinished and nothing wakes the agent. Do not build parallel orphan detection: a dead bridge already classifies as `side_effect_uncertain` or `owner_lost_host_restart`, which `recovery-controller sweep` handles.

**A detached bridge inherits none of the Zo turn's environment.** The prompt's first step must run `set -a; . /root/.zo_secrets; set +a` before any step that reads an API key.

**Delivery must come from inside the bridge** via `mcp__zo__send_email_to_user` (or the relevant Zo MCP tool). The automation's `delivery_method` only reports what the ~1 s Zo turn produced, which is one status line. Never rely on it for output.

**Converting an existing automation:** use `python3 /home/workspace/Skills/automation-resilience/scripts/convert-to-bridge.py --automation-id <uuid> --job <job>` (dry-run by default, `--apply` to commit). It splits the instruction at the contract marker, writes the prompt file, backs up the original instruction, and re-asserts `next_run`.

**Verify every time, in this order:** (a) `next_run` is non-null after create/edit — a null `next_run` on an `active=True` automation is a silently dead schedule; (b) never use `COUNT=1` for a one-shot, since Zo's normalizer drops BYHOUR/BYMINUTE and consumes the lone occurrence — arm a plain recurring rule and delete it after the observed fire; (c) after the first real fire, confirm a receipt under `/home/workspace/.zo/cli-bridge-runs/` whose `outcome` is `ok`, and confirm delivery independently (mailbox, file, or queue state), not from the bridge's own self-report. Judge a run by `outcome`, never by `exit_code` alone: a clean CLI exit with the contract still `in_progress` is `ended_mid_contract`, which is a failure. `automation-resilience.ts status` needs the FULL automation UUID — an 8-char prefix returns `{"exists":false}` and looks identical to a run that never happened.

**Keep an automation on the plain Zo path only when** its entire run is one short model turn: no /zo/ask dispatch, no consensus panel or MoA lineup, no queue drain, no repo mutation, and total runtime comfortably under the 120 s per-call ceiling. Short, cheap automations gain nothing from the bridge. When in doubt, bridge it.

Prerequisites already satisfied on this host and required for any new bridge job: `IS_SANDBOX=1` must be exported before spawning `claude -p` (everything runs as root and Claude Code otherwise refuses `--dangerously-skip-permissions`), and the `zo` MCP server must be reachable to the bridge so it can call Zo tools.

**Converting older automations:** two contract shapes exist. Newer instructions carry the `<!-- AUTOMATION RESILIENCE CONTRACT v1 -->` HTML-comment markers; older ones carry the same contract in plain text ending in "The original automation instruction begins immediately after this contract." The converter splits on either, and refuses to touch the automation when neither boundary is present or the body after it is under 200 characters. Do not add a `--preflight` while converting unless the automation already had a skip condition — that changes when it does nothing, which is a behavior change, not a hosting change.

**Drift watch:** `[SYS] Audit Bridge Conformance` (`4de40924-7880-4688-b01a-ad6ff110855e`) runs weekly Monday 07:40 Arizona, itself bridge-hosted, and emails only when a new conversion candidate, a dead schedule, or a bridge→Zo-hosted regression appears against `/home/workspace/.zo/automation-bridge-baseline.json`.
